 Order

This petition is filed under Section 439 Cr.P.C. to enlarge the petitioner/accused No.1 on bail in Cr.No.553/2023 registered at Bellanduru Police Station, Bengaluru City, for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 304B r/w 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

2. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner, the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent- State and perused the material on record.
3.
In brief, the case of the prosecution is that deceased Shravani is the wife of the petitioner/accused No.1.
Accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents of accused No.1.
The marriage of Shravani was performed with the petitioner on 15.10.2021 at V.R.Kalyana Mantap, BEML Nagar, KGF.
As per the demand of the accused, 150 grams of gold ornaments were given as dowry and marriage was performed spending about Rs.18 lakhs.
After the marriage, the deceased was residing along with accused Nos.1 to 3, in her matrimonial home situated at House no.53, I Cross, II Main, H.P.Nagar, Bangarpet, Kolar District.
For about 3-4 months, she was looked after properly.
Thereafter, the accused persons started subjecting her to physical and mental torture in connection with dowry.
They were abusing the deceased that no sufficient dowry was given and the gold ornaments which were given are not of good quality.
The accused were also demanding a new bike.
On 24.09.2023, the deceased was driven out of her matrimonial home and since then she was residing in her parental home in Bengaluru.
Even thereafter, the petitioner/accused No.1 was subjecting her to mental torture by calling her over phone and demanding dowry.

Unable to bear the physical and mental torture, Shravani committed suicide by hanging herself in her parental home on 09.11.2023.
4.
Complaint is lodged by the father of the deceased.

In his complaint, he has alleged that the NC:
2024:KHC:6764 accused has demanded a motorcycle and 250 grams of gold ornaments as dowry.
However, 150 grams of gold ornaments were given and marriage was performed by spending Rs.18 lakhs.

It is alleged that the petitioner and his parents were subjecting the deceased to physical and mental torture on the ground that the gold ornaments given were not of good quality and the motorcycle was not provided etc.
5.

The learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the deceased is from Bengaluru and since there was no compatibility in the marriage, she returned to her parental home on 24.09.2023 and she was staying along with her parents.
He contended that she has committed suicide in her parental home and there is no material to show that she was subjected to mental torture in connection with dowry prior to her death.

sentences.text: The learned High Court Government Pleader has contended that there is sufficient material to show NC: 2024:KHC:6764 that the deceased was being subjected to physical and mental torture by the accused persons and this petitioner, being her husband has made telephone calls to the deceased and tortured her mentally by demanding motorcycle etc.

He contends that the death has taken place within seven years of marriage and in view of the material collected, there is a prima facie case against the petitioner.
7
Admittedly, the deceased has committed suicide in her parental home on 09.11.023 by hanging herself.
According to the prosecution, she came to her parental home from her matrimonial home on 24.09.2023.
It is not alleged that between the said period the petitioner had visited the house of the deceased in Bengaluru.
The prosecution is alleging that he was making telephone calls to the deceased and torturing her to get a motorbike.
No material is placed to show that on the date of incident he had called the deceased over phone.
The prosecution has to establish that she was subjected to cruelty by the NC: 2024:KHC:6764 accused before her death.
Accused Nos.2 and 3 are enlarged on bail in Crl.P.No.13390/2023 vide order dated 16.01.2024.
The petitioner is in judicial custody since 10.11.2023.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed.
Petitioner has undertaken to furnish adequate surety to ensure his presence before the trial court.
Hence, by imposing necessary conditions, the petitioner can be admitted to bail.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i. Petition is allowed.

Ii Petitioner shall be released on bail in Crime No.553/2023 of Bellanduru Police Station, Bengaluru City, pending in CC No.3570/2024 on the file of 41st Additional CMM Court, Bangalore City, subject to following conditions:
1. He shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum NC: 2024:KHC:6764 to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
2. He shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court, if there is any change in address.
3. He shall not directly or indirectly tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
4. He shall appear before the Trial Court regularly without fail.
